comment: Where the mega structures stand (tools/terrain_lab/world_features.py -> <world>_features.json, drawn by terrain_core/props). Models: assets/terrain_core/props (tools/blender/terrain_props.py). `spires`: the canyon steppe's kilometre spires, on the canyon floors, their tops at the level of the high ground round them (the steppe islands, the plateau's rim) within `reach_km`. `bridges`: natural bridges between spires whose tops are alike. `groups`: megaliths by zone, made mega by `height_m`. `singles`: one of a kind. `material`: a ground material (content/config/terrain_core/biomes.json) laid over a kind in world space; otherwise the slope material of the biome it stands in. Sections: `terrain` (large terrain parts), `megaliths`, `buildings` (off); each instance is tagged with its section as `cat`.

terrain.comment: Large parts of the terrain that are meshes (tools/terrain_lab/world_terrain_parts.py): the canyon's spires with its bridges, rises and ledges, clefts, sea stacks, floating isles, sentinel peaks, and rock forms by zone. The cliff walls are under `cliffs`.

satellites.comment: lesser pinnacles round each big one: count, distance in the big one's radii, height as a share of its rise; ground under them no steeper than slope_max, gap_m clear of other feet

spires.comment_sites: sites 'relief': the pinnacles stand on the remnants steppe_relief.py found (spur ends, bays at side valleys' mouths, <world>_steppe_relief.json) with their tops from there; otherwise drawn on the canyon floor by the rules here

spire_islands.comment: Small islands on the spires at different heights, bridged to each other and to the steppe islands (the heart of the canyon biome).

canyon_islands.comment: The canyon's mesa islands: rims lined with spire-like boulder rock; between neighbours, spires of every size carrying bridges and ribbons.

canyon_debris.comment: heaps of broken slabs round the canyon's pinnacles and the buttes (steppe_relief.json): per_100m of the host's radius (count limits), in a ring of `*_ring` radii out from its axis, scaled by the host (host_per_scale_m of radius a unit, `scale` limits), sunk `sink` of their height; dropped where the ground falls more than max_fall of their height under them

terrain.comment_off: 14.10 (user): bridges, ribbons, platforms, switchbacks, rim ledges and the canyon islands' bridges are off (enabled false, bridges.share 0, spires.rise_share 0) while the pinnacles and columns themselves are worked out

megaliths.comment: Megaliths (tools/terrain_lab/world_megaliths.py): one kind per biome, none repeated elsewhere; the isles and the crescent have none. `heroes`: zone -> {kind, count, share of the biome's extent as height}. `prism_row`: towering prisms along a border (none now: the marshes have A-1). `cube_cluster`: huge white cubes. `coast_spikes`: spikes all along a coast. `groups` / `singles`: as elsewhere. `a1_monoliths`: the giant slabs A-1 in loose rows on the dry ground of the marshes (world_megaliths.a1_monoliths; rows, spacing and scale from the asset manifest; the slab is drawn in its own material, "look"). The golden desert's one magic megalith is the gate A-3 (world_gate.py, rules in its asset manifest), no hero there.

marsh_islands.comment: The marshes' layout (tools/terrain_lab/marsh_islands.py, before world_features.py; marshes/MARSHES_REQUIREMENTS.md). `landform`: the shallow floor - water at `water_level_m`, pools `water_depth_m` deep covering `wet_share` of it in patches of `pool_km`, hummocks `hummock_m`. `monoliths`: `count` A-1 slabs at `scale` over the whole valley, at least `edge_m` inside it and `gap_m` apart, each on a flat pad `pad_height_m` over the water, `pad_margin_m` wider than its foot, eased into the ground over `pad_blend_m`. `hills` and `islets`: `per_km2`, `gap_m` apart, `steps` risers making `top_m` (each at least `riser_min_m`), treads `tread_m`, top radius `r_top_m`, outline wobbling by `wobble`; on `cliff_sides` sectors `cliff_width_deg` wide the treads shrink by `cliff_squeeze` (one cliff into the water); a hill with `ramp` has one sector `ramp_width_deg` wide with gentle steps. `checks`: the water's share over `window_m` windows should lie in `water_share`. `forest_pools`: red pools in the forest's edge, `wet_share` of it at the border thinning to none `width_m` in, only where the slope is under `max_slope`. The hills' steps are meshes (marsh_hill_mesh.py, `mesh_sink_m`, `mesh_rough_m`); the ground under them is raised `ground_inset_m` inside their outline. With `riser_m` each step is its own height in that range (user 13.10: 0.3-0.7 of a man's height). User 13.10 (v6): the floor rolls (`landform.roll_m` over `roll_km`, easing out at the pools); `hills` are mounds (`mound`: `height_m`, a domed top of `top_radius_m` falling by `dome`, a raw flank `flank_m`, rough `noise_m`) worn down by thermal erosion (`erosion`: slopes over `talus` slide, `iterations` x `rate`, on a `fine_m` grid), and their worn tops cut into `steps` terraces of `riser_m` by the ground's contours (no more than `terrace_share` of the hill, treads at least `min_tread_m`); `knolls` are the same mounds, lower and grassy. User 13.10 (v8): the hills' terraces are fine relief, not meshes (`hills.relief`: the ground at `texel_m` a texel, risers `riser_width_m` wide, wall lines wandering `wander_m` over `wander_scale_m`, treads uneven by `tread_noise_m`, eased into the hill over `blend_m`; <world>_relief.bin, src/terrain_core/relief.hpp). User 13.10 (v10): natural benches, not rings - the steps run along `relief.sectors` flanks of `sector_deg` each, every step its own stretch (`stagger`), tapering out over `end_deg`. User 13.10 (v11): hills and knolls are islands rising gently out of the water (`mound`: `radius_m`, a crest `crest_offset` of the way towards one side, long and easy behind it, steeper below it); a hill's benches only on that steep side (`relief.sector_deg`). v11b: the benches lie part way down the steep side, the highest at `hills.top_share` of the way from the water up to the crest.

buildings.comment: Buildings (tools/terrain_lab/world_buildings.py): their own piece of work, off until then.

cliffs.comment: Cliff walls over the steep bands (tools/terrain_lab/world_cliffs.py), built as one solid so walls that meet merge instead of crossing: `zones`: zone -> slope (rise over run) from which ground is a wall there, or {slope, coast_m}: only within coast_m of the sea. A wall must drop `min_drop_m` within `band_m`. Each height of it reaches out downhill until it stands, `overhang` more at the rim, never less than `min_push_m` (where the ground is already sheer) plus `overhang_drop` of its drop at the rim, and past its foot never more than `gap_share` of half the floor in front of it (a gully keeps a floor); `strata`, `gullies` and `rock_noise_m` shape its face, `smooth_cells` rounds the corners of its outline; `sink_m`: how deep the surface lies under the ground away from the walls; `skirt_m`: how far the tile borders hang down (no cracks between tiles at different detail); `apron_m`: how far below the foot scree is banked against the wall, `scree_share` of the drop high (at most `scree_max_m`). Colours: a wall wears the biome on top of it (world_biomes.png, looked for `biome_look_m` past its top), its lowest `foot_share` and its scree the biome at its foot: per biome of biomes.json its slope material on the walls unless `materials` names another, its ground on what faces up, its tint, `moss` on its rock.

styles.comment: per biome of biomes.json, the face of its walls: `strata` ledges' strength, `strata_m` a bed (its period is 2 pi of it), `slab` how much a bed is a slab (lip at its top, undercut below) rather than a wave, `gullies` runnels, `flutes` deep vertical grooves (cells of `flute_m`), `overhang` and `overhang_drop` as the cliffs' own (0: the wall stands straight, user 14.10 for the canyon); the user's canyon references doc/NewRef/steppe
